motive: To delay discovery of the changed destination while keeping the appearance that the approved reserve payment was merely retried.
method: After his destination edit on PAY-712 was denied he created PAY-712B, used a successful manual override, reused APR-103 and sent the same ₹12,000 to a different destination fingerprint, then called it a routine retry.
explanation: The records prove a changed destination and a cover story. They do not identify the real-world account holder or what happened to the money after settlement.

timeline.event: Dev’s attempt to edit the destination of PAY-712 is denied
The gateway rejects PAY-712 on destination validation
Dev’s manual override succeeds; PAY-712 is reversed
Dev writes that the replacement was a routine retry

causal_chain: The original payment was rejected on destination validation and reversed.
Dev created a replacement under the same approval and overrode the controls.
The replacement went to a different destination fingerprint.
His note calls it a routine retry, which the changed fingerprint contradicts.

resolution.motive: To hide the changed destination behind a routine-retry story.
resolution.method: He used a manual override to route the replacement to a different destination under an approval that covered the original destination.
chain: PAY-712B was created by Dev (request record and audit).
A successful MANUAL_OVERRIDE sits on PAY-712B.
The fingerprint changed from DEST-NORTH-44 to DEST-NORTH-84.
APR-103 covers the original payee and purpose and does not authorise a changed destination.
